decisions.reason: As a recently launched handle family that fits the firm's core architectural hardware range, its market potential is still being learned and the cost of keeping it available is likely modest relative to its option value.
This mitred handle family is somewhat more niche and overlaps with other new handle lines, but its differentiated design still justifies staying on the market while demand uncertainty resolves.
A multifunctional lever handle matches the firm's barrier-free and compliance-oriented positioning, so management would likely preserve this option until clearer evidence of weak adoption appears.
Because it is another new lever-handle family in a crowded launch set, it faces some portfolio-pruning risk, but there is not yet enough evidence of poor value realization to warrant withdrawal.
Its standalone presentation and German Design Award are strong early positive signals, making it very likely that management continues backing this collection.
A new finish can be dropped more easily than a full product family if uptake disappoints and complexity costs rise, but for now it remains a relatively low-cost option worth keeping.
